attestations.notes: Sound. Separation inside an arbitrary existing set with the contradiction z != z produces a set with no members, and Extensionality proves uniqueness; all three cited dependency statements match their uses.
Sound. Nonemptiness supplies B in x, Separation constructs the common-member subset of B, and B in x makes the extra z in B condition redundant; Extensionality proves independence of B.
Sound. The weak Power Set axiom supplies an ambient set containing every subset, Separation trims it to exactly the subsets of x, and Extensionality gives uniqueness.

Sound. Each of the five identities follows from the exact membership clauses for union, nonempty intersection, singleton, and unordered pair; the pair and singleton intersection cases explicitly satisfy nonemptiness.
Sound. From a in A and b in B, both {a} and {a,b} lie in P(A union B), so the Kuratowski pair is a subset of that power set and hence lies in the double power set.

Sound. The proof handles the degenerate a=b case separately and exhausts the a!=b alternatives; both directions of the biconditional and the singleton specialization follow from the cited pair-membership and Extensionality clauses.

Sound. Applying unordered-pair equality to the two Kuratowski pairs gives the two exhaustive matchings, and both the ordinary and degenerate singleton cases force a=c and b=d; the reverse direction is immediate from the definition.
Sound. Two unions of R contain both coordinates of every Kuratowski pair in R, after which Separation yields exactly the domain and range classes and their asserted inclusions.
Sound. Infinity supplies I0, Separation inside I0 constructs the elements common to every inductive set, closure under successor is checked, and mutual inclusion plus Extensionality gives uniqueness.

Sound. A subset containing 0 and closed under successor is inductive, so minimality of omega gives the reverse inclusion; the property form is the corresponding separated subset of N and both formulations are proved.

Sound. The simultaneous induction proves successor transitivity and rules out sigma(n) in sigma(n) in both possible membership branches, using only the inductive hypotheses n transitive and n notin n.

Sound, with a nonfatal sub-30-second set-formation omission: step 1.1 suppresses the Power Set/Separation construction of the set of closed subsets of N x A before intersecting it. The minimal-closed-relation totality, single-valuedness, recursion equations, and uniqueness argument are otherwise complete, and P1/P2/P3 are used faithfully.
Sound. P3 is the induction theorem, P1 follows because sigma(n) contains n, and P2 follows from transitivity and irreflexivity after excluding the m=n branch; all Peano clauses are covered.

Sound. Recursion on the Peano system gives a unique total s_m for each m and its equations, and the pointwise assignment defines the claimed total binary operation; the routine Separation construction of its graph is implicit but closes immediately.
Sound. The base and successor step use exactly the two recursive clauses for addition, and induction proves the left identity; the right identity is correctly identified as definitional.
Sound. Induction on the second argument proves sigma(m)+n=sigma(m+n), including the n=0 boundary, using only the cited addition recursion and induction principle.
Sound. The n=0 case uses the proved left identity and the successor step matches the recursive right-successor law with the cited left-successor law; induction closes for arbitrary m.
Sound. Induction on c checks the zero endpoint and rewrites both sides at sigma(c) by the addition recursion; no unstated commutativity is used.
Sound. Induction on the common right summand reduces the successor case by the cited injectivity of sigma and then applies the inductive hypothesis.
Sound. The inductively defined subset contains 0 and every successor directly, yielding the exhaustive zero-or-successor dichotomy and hence the nonzero form.

Sound. The proof separately establishes incompatibility of equality and the two strict directions, then proves comparability by induction; the m>n successor branch correctly splits the nonzero gap as sigma(a), including a=0.

Sound. Reflexivity and transitivity follow from the additive definition, totality from trichotomy, and antisymmetry from the zero-sum argument plus cancellation; every cited arithmetic lemma states the used clause.

Sound. A nonzero additive gap is a successor, giving the forward implication, while the reverse implication uses successor-left arithmetic and cancellation to exclude equality; the immediate-successor consequence follows in both directions.

Sound. Coordinates of each relation pair lie in the intrinsic domain and range, and both directions of the A x B criterion follow from the exact Cartesian-product and ordered-pair characterisation statements.
Sound. For fixed m, addition by m is a total endomap of N, so recursion supplies the unique p_m and both multiplication clauses; assembling the pointwise binary graph is routine and implicit.

Sound. Associativity and commutativity transport an additive witness through translation, cancellation gives the converse, and the same cancellation equivalence handles both directions of strict compatibility.

Sound. Each claimed collection is separated inside the stated Cartesian-product or relation ambient set, and the coordinate bounds follow from the exact domain/range definitions; empty relations cause no problem.
Sound. The right unit is a direct recursion calculation and the simultaneous induction proves 0*n=0 and 1*n=n, including n=0; all addition identities used are cited.

Sound. The first induction proves left distributivity and the nested induction in step 1.3 proves the successor-left law with explicit base and successor algebra. The second induction is compressed into one numbered step but is a nonfatal presentation compression, not a missing mathematical case.
Sound. Induction on n matches the multiplication recursion to the previously proved successor-left law, with the zero case supplied by the cited identity lemma.
Sound. Induction on c reduces the successor case to left distributivity and the multiplication recursion; the zero boundary is explicitly checked.
Sound. For nonzero m,n the successor representations make mn itself a successor, so Peano P1 excludes zero; this proves the exact contrapositive and hence the stated implication.

Sound. Right distributivity transports the additive order witness, and with a nonzero multiplier the no-zero-divisors lemma makes the new gap nonzero; cancellation rules out equality for the strict conclusion.
Sound. The two representative-equivalence equations add and regroup to the equivalence equation for sums, while commuting the first equation gives the exact swapped-pair equation for negation.

Sound. Factoring against the first representative equivalence yields the required product-pair equivalence, and symmetry of the product formula legitimately repeats the argument for the second factor.

Sound. Representative independence is cited first, and the subsequent coordinate calculations verify the additive abelian-group laws, multiplicative commutative-monoid laws, distributivity, and the explicit additive inverse.

Sound with one nonfatal sub-30-second omission: reflexivity of the integer order is not numbered, although x<=x follows immediately from a+b=b+a in the displayed representative definition. Well-definedness is proved in both representative directions; totality, antisymmetry, transitivity, translation invariance, and positive-product closure are otherwise established.
Sound. Peano P1 gives the zero base and injectivity of successor converts equality at the successor stage into the forbidden inductive-hypothesis equality.

Sound. The proof first establishes transitivity of N, then proves m<sigma(n) iff m<=n, proves membership/order in both directions by induction, and derives inclusion/order plus the zero and successor corollaries; every advertised clause and boundary is covered without ordinal input.

Sound. Trichotomy exhausts the nonzero sign patterns, ordered-ring positive-product closure and elementary sign identities exclude a zero product, and distributivity reduces multiplicative cancellation to that result.
Sound. Distributivity applied to 0+0 and additive cancellation give 0*a=0; the field definition on disk explicitly supplies multiplication and identity laws on all of F, including zero.

Sound. The two cross-product equalities are combined by commutative-ring algebra to give exactly the representative relations for product and sum, and negation follows by multiplying the equality by -1.

Sound. Fixed-representative calculations verify every field axiom; integer no-zero-divisors keeps all constructed denominators nonzero and licenses the cancellation in distributivity, while a nonzero numerator supplies the reciprocal.

Sound. Assuming no least member, the separated initial-avoidance set T contains 0 and is successor-closed, so induction forces T=N and contradicts nonemptiness. The discrete predecessor calculation and all endpoint cases are explicit.

Sound with two nonfatal sub-30-second omissions: the representative-independence calculation writes only the unprimed-to-primed implication (the reverse is the identical argument with the representatives swapped), and reflexivity ad<=ad is not separately numbered. The scaling lemma, totality, antisymmetry, transitivity, translation invariance, and positive products are correct.
Sound. Translation preserves the same positive difference, and the difference for the sum of two inequalities is the sum of two positive differences, exactly using ordered-field O2.

Sound. The transposition normalisation makes an alleged injection sigma(sigma(n))->sigma(n) restrict to the induction-forbidden sigma(n)->n map. Claims 2-5 then follow by restriction, inverse bijections, and the explicit missing-point transposition; zero, successor, proper-subset, and single-choice cases are all handled.

Sound. Distributivity and zero multiplication identify (-a)b and a(-b) as additive inverses of ab, then inverse uniqueness yields (-a)(-b)=ab; the cited field item records the needed inverse-uniqueness consequence.

Sound. Positive-cone closure and the proved negative-product identities give all three sign cases and both forward monotonicity laws; trichotomy excludes the other two alternatives for each converse, so both iff directions hold.
Sound. Trichotomy for a nonzero element leaves exactly the positive and negative cases, positive-cone multiplication handles each, and (-a)(-a)=a^2 closes the negative case.
Sound. The field axiom 1!=0 and identity 1^2=1 make the nonzero-square lemma apply directly, yielding 0<1.
Sound. Standard abelian-group calculations prove uniqueness of additive identity and inverses, and the same argument in the nonzero multiplicative group proves uniqueness of 1 and nonzero inverses.

Sound. A positive element's nonzero inverse cannot be negative because its product would make 1 negative, and multiplying 0<a<b by the positive product a^{-1}b^{-1} gives the strict reciprocal reversal.

Mathematically sound, with a nonfatal citation-completeness omission: the two inductions and the identities m(n+1)=mn+m and (m+n)+1=m+(n+1) use the natural-number induction/addition/multiplication interfaces without declaring them in deps or Facts. The proof writes the needed base and successor calculations, and the omission is repaired by the standard three published natural-arithmetic citations.

Sound. The sign cases prove multiplicativity, the two inequalities u<=|u| and -u<=|u| give the triangle inequality, and applying it in both directions gives the reverse triangle inequality. Nonfatally, L1 packages the elementary consequence (-u)v=-(uv) under the ordered-field citation rather than citing the dedicated sign lemma.

Sound after one nonfatal endpoint convention: because the sequence is indexed from 1 while a Cauchy witness is merely N in the naturals, step 1.1 should replace N by max(N,1) before using a_N. This is a sub-30-second adjustment; the tail triangle bound and finite-prefix maximum then prove the Statement exactly.

Sound. Termwise rational laws give all ring axioms, epsilon/2 proves closure under addition and negation, and boundedness plus delta=epsilon/(A+B) proves product closure; zero and one constant sequences are covered.

Sound. The epsilon/2 null bound and triangle inequality establish the Cauchy condition. Nonfatally, A2 is worded as though it were an assumption even though it is used only as the recognition criterion from def-rational-cauchy-sequence; the proof does not actually assume the conclusion.

Sound with one nonfatal omitted boundary sentence: step 4.1 calls the additive subgroup nonempty without explicitly observing that the zero sequence is null. Sum and negation closure are proved by epsilon/2, and bounded Cauchy multiplication gives ideal absorption via epsilon/B.

Sound. The representative relation proves injectivity, the integer operation formulas preserve addition and multiplication, and the representative order gives order preservation and the exact nonnegative image with uniqueness. Nonfatally, A1/A2 aggregate the declared integer and natural definitions without attaching their individual citation labels.
